slice3.tolerance_decision_for_lead: Non-separable family is ill-conditioned next to its clip boundaries (colour over white: Lum = 1 +- 1 ulp, clip scale (1-l)/(x-l) divides by a near-zero). An independent f32/f64 emulation of pigment's own algorithm differs from exact f64 by up to 1.6e-6 at the worst lattice pixels (same value as the vulkan lattice maximum), so a GPU-vs-pigment difference of 1.1e-6 to 1.6e-6 there is input conditioning, not a formula difference. The 1e-6 per-layer budget of slice 1-2 therefore does not hold for hue/saturation/colour/luminosity on knife-edge inputs; the asserted bound for them is 2e-6 per composite. Random tiles and hand pixels stay at 5e-7 or less.
slice3.knife_edges: Discontinuous cases: non-separable set_sat at exactly equal channels (gray) and whole-pixel / hard_mix thresholds are decided by exact comparisons. They are bit-identical to the CPU when the backdrop enters bit-exact (first layer, tile backdrops: lattice proves this). On a GPU-derived backdrop that is within 1 ulp of gray / a threshold the GPU may take the other branch than the CPU (same caveat as colour_burn/dodge in slice 2); validators must not use such inputs as a parity oracle.
